literal: " Shortly afterward he was further appointed Guard General, Commandant of the Capital Garrison, Minister of Sacrifices, and Opening-Establishment Equal-in-Rank to the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: " Shortly afterward he was further appointed guard general, commandant of the capital garrison, minister of sacrifices, and opening-establishment equal in rank to the three dukes.

literal: Because Qinghe territory lay within the capital region, his title was changed to Prince of Le'an.
idiomatic: Because Qinghe lay within the capital region, he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Le'an.

literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and sent out as Executive-office Vice Director at Shuozhou.
idiomatic: He was made palace attendant and right vice director of the Masters of Writing, then sent out as executive-office vice director at Shuozhou.

literal: When Houzhu was defeated at Jinyang, the Empress Dowager returned to the capital by the Tumen Road; an edict ordered Mai to take overall command of troops and escort the Empress Dowager.
idiomatic: When Houzhu was defeated at Jinyang, the Empress Dowager returned to the capital by the Tumen Road; an edict put Mai in overall command of troops to escort her.

literal: At that time favored eunuchs still carried out wanton cruelty; throughout the common folk they set hawks and dogs to seize chickens and pigs by force.
idiomatic: Favored eunuchs still ran riot; they loosed hawks and dogs on the people's chickens and pigs and took them by force.

literal: Mai seized Equal-in-Rank Third Rank official Gou Ziyi and paraded him through the army, intending a mass execution.
idiomatic: Mai seized Gou Ziyi, an official of equal-in-rank third rank, paraded him before the army, and meant to execute him on the spot.

literal: Only after the Empress Dowager issued an order was he released.
idiomatic: Only when the Empress Dowager sent an order was Gou released.

literal: Liu Wenshu whispered to Mai, saying, "Men like Ziyi can make or break us with a word — how can you treat them thus? Will you not fear slander afterward?
idiomatic: Liu Wenshu whispered to Mai, "Men like Ziyi can make or break us with a word — how can you treat them so? Will you not fear what men will say afterward?

literal: " Mai rolled up his sleeves and said to Wenshu, "Since the Shenwu Emperor, we have nurtured soldiers, entrusted government to kin and worthies, and taken the field in war — never once were we defeated.
idiomatic: " Mai rolled up his sleeves and told Wenshu, "Since Gao Huan, we have nurtured soldiers, entrusted rule to kin and worthies, and taken the field — never once were we broken.

literal: Now the western invaders have reached Bingzhou; many high officials have already defected. It is precisely because these men monopolize power and manipulate affairs that hearts within and without have split and the gentry have fallen apart.
idiomatic: Now the western invaders stand at Bingzhou; great officials defect in droves. It is because men like these hold power and twist affairs that court and countryside have lost heart and the gentry have come undone.

literal: If I can behead this one today, and die tomorrow for it, I shall have no regret.
idiomatic: If I can cut off this man's head today and die for it tomorrow, I will not regret it.

literal: Your house and mine are joined by marriage — we must share the same hatred of evil. To speak thus against me — is this what I expected of you!
idiomatic: Our houses are joined by marriage; we ought to hate the same evil. To speak to me like this — is this what I expected of you!

literal: " When the Empress Dowager returned to Ye, Zhou armies pressed on in succession; everyone was panic-stricken, with no will to fight; court officials surrendered by day and night without cease.
idiomatic: " When the Empress Dowager reached Ye, Zhou armies pressed on without pause; panic spread and no one would fight; court officials surrendered day and night without end.

literal: Mai therefore memorialized Houzhu, saying, "Those who have defected are mostly nobles; among the common soldiers, many have not yet turned.
idiomatic: Mai therefore memorialized Houzhu: "Those who have turned are mostly nobles; among the common ranks many have not yet gone over.

literal: I ask that the families of all officials of fifth rank and above be gathered and placed in the Three Platforms, and that they be told: 'If the battle is not won, we will withdraw and burn the platforms.'
idiomatic: I ask that the families of every official of fifth rank and above be gathered into the Three Platforms, and that they be told: 'If we do not win, we withdraw and burn the platforms.'

literal: " These men, cherishing wife and children, will surely fight to the death.
idiomatic: " Those men, for wife and child, will fight to the death.

literal: Moreover our armies have repeatedly retreated north; the enemy despises us. If we stake everything on a single battle behind the walls, reason says we must break them — this too is the supreme stratagem.
idiomatic: Our armies have retreated again and again; the enemy holds us cheap. One decisive battle with our backs to the wall must break them — that too is the highest plan.

literal: " Houzhu in the end could not adopt it.
idiomatic: " Houzhu in the end would not take his counsel.

literal: When Qi fell he entered Zhou; by precedent he was given an Opening Establishment.
idiomatic: When Qi fell he entered Zhou and, by precedent, was granted an opening establishment.

literal: Under the Sui he successively held the governorships of Yang, Chu, Guang, and Tao Provinces.
idiomatic: Under the Sui he served in turn as governor of Yang, Chu, Guang, and Tao provinces.

literal: He died in the Kaihuang era.
idiomatic: He died in the Kaihuang era.

literal: The historian writes: The Changes says, "Heaven and earth wax and wane; they advance and retreat with the times — how much more so with men!
idiomatic: The historian writes: The Changes says, "Heaven and earth fill and empty; they rise and fall with the season — how much more is this true of men!

literal: " For obstruction and opening have their appointed seasons; debasement and elevation follow the Way.
idiomatic: " For passage and blockage have their season; decline and ascent follow the Way.

literal: When all the world yearns for order, then show benevolence to meet it;
idiomatic: When the world longs for order, show humane rule to answer it;

literal: when petty men hold the path, then practice restrained virtue to escape harm.
idiomatic: when petty men hold the road, practice restrained virtue to slip clear of harm.

literal: As for one who bears a Huo Guang's design yet stands in a screen-barricade place — if he wishes to lose the state and defy adversity, can he succeed?
idiomatic: But for one who holds a Huo Guang's map yet stands as a screen for the realm — if he would lose the state and turn from hardship, can he succeed?

literal: Zhao Commandery, with the closeness of stem and calyx, bore the weight of a deathbed charge: to step aside in a high bow would have endangered the altars; to remove evil would have brought peace to men and gods alike.
idiomatic: Zhao Commandery, close as stem to calyx, bore a deathbed charge of grave weight: to yield the high seat would have endangered the altars; to purge evil would have brought peace to men and gods alike.

literal: Thus he rested upon single-hearted virtue, shared this steadfast heart, trod a perilous road without doubt, and faced crisis without fear.
idiomatic: So he anchored himself in one virtue, kept one steadfast heart, walked a perilous road without wavering, and met crisis without fear.

literal: With such loyalty and righteousness, he could have seized and killed the wicked minister Yin.
idiomatic: With loyalty and righteousness such as this, he could have seized and killed Yin the wicked.

literal: Yet if his virtue shone over the four seas, he did not meet the clarity of King Cheng of Zhou;
idiomatic: Yet though his virtue might have lit the four seas, he did not meet a King Cheng of Zhou;

literal: rather it was as when the court lost the Three Worthies — in the end he saw the calamity of the Yin ruins.
idiomatic: rather, as when a court loses its three worthies, he lived to see the ruin of Yin.

literal: Otherwise how could the state perish so swiftly, as though at a shadow's touch!
idiomatic: Otherwise how could the state have withered so fast — as if at a shadow's touch!

literal: Qinghe met the season of founding the realm, rose to the blue clouds by his own efforts, went out as general and in as minister, aiding the great enterprise — not even Liu Jia of Han nor Cao Hong of Wei suffice to measure higher or lower against him.
idiomatic: Qinghe came up in the age of founding, climbed to the blue clouds by his own strength, went out as general and in as minister, and helped raise the great enterprise — not even Han's Liu Jia nor Wei's Cao Hong can be set above or below him.

literal: Tianbao was an ill-starred time, easy to breed regret and blame; yet one cannot hide his heroic stature — it only throws into relief the Founding Ancestor's fault and virtue alike.
idiomatic: Tianbao was an ill hour, quick to breed regret and blame; yet his heroic stature cannot be hidden — it only throws Gao Yang's fault and his virtue into sharper light.

literal: Appraisal: Zhao Commandery — heroic and grand; bearing and mien composed and upright.
idiomatic: Appraisal: Zhao Commandery — heroic and grand; bearing composed, mien upright.

literal: Heaven's Way is without partiality; such a man, such a fate.
idiomatic: Heaven's Way shows no favor; such a man, such a fate.

literal: Illustrious Qinghe — by him the state was ordered.
idiomatic: Illustrious Qinghe — by him the state was governed.

literal: A small stain at the final road — not a ruin of virtue.
idiomatic: A small flaw at the end of the road — not a collapse of virtue.

literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
